notes.claim: A line needs an arrow from the origin to a point on it and an arrow parallel to it; a plane has a normal arrow perpendicular to it.
A rotating laser's receiver shows by its arrows whether it is above or below the beam, and digital-readout models show how far from on-grade it is (i3 analogy).

sources.title: Lines and Planes
sources.quote: The key idea related to equations of lines is you always need to have a vector, say x 0 , from the origin to a point of the line and a vector, say v , parallel to the line

sources.title: Lines and Planes
sources.quote: Every plane has a vector orthogonal (perpendicular) to it, called a normal vector and usually denoted by the letter n

sources.title: Spectra HL700 Laser Receiver - Advanced Elevation Readout
sources.quote: The readout is displayed on the large front and rear LCD’s and shows exactly how far the elevation is from on-grade.
